questions.question: Who among the following considered "Right to Constitutional Remedies" to be the heart and soul of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct, i.e. __**Dr. B R Ambedkar.**__

__
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar__.
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as; __Right to Constitutional Remedies__.

 
 

 __Article__
 __Consists of__
 
 

 Article 32
 
 
Right to move the Supreme court for the enforcement of fundamental rights including the writs.

 
 
• habeas corpus
 
• mandamus
 
• prohibition
 
• certiorari
 
• quo warranto
 
 
 
 

Extra facts:

 
• Habeas Corpus: This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained whether in prison or in private custody, before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
 
• Mandamus: The writ of command is issued by supreme or high court when any government, court, corporation, or any public authority has to do a public duty but fails to do so.
 
• Prohibition: A court that is higher in position issues a Prohibition writ against a court that is lower in position to prevent the latter from exceeding its jurisdiction or usurping a jurisdiction that it does not possess. It directs inactivity.
 
• Certiorari: The writ of certiorari can be issued by the supreme or high court for quashing the order already passed by an inferior court, tribunal or quasi-judicial authority.
 
• Quo-Warranto: The writ of quo-warranto can be issued by the supreme or high court for asking of by what authority or warrant. It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office.

questions.question: Which countries are separated by the Mac Mohan Line?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __India-China__**

The Mac Mohan Line is the international boundary line between India and China and it was proposed by Henry Mac Mohan in 1914.

The McMahon Line marks the boundary between the China-occupied territory of the East-Himalayan region and the Indian regions.

This region is a mountainous place of high altitude.

This line was determined by Sir Henry McMahon, a British Foreign Secretary in British India, and it is called the McMahon Line after his name.

The total length of this line is 890 kilometers.

questions.question: Brain receives and sends signals in the form of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrical impulses**__.

The basic unit of the brain is the neuron and neurons exchange signals in the form of electrical impulses through axons and dendrites.

The detailed process is:

__
 
• The receptor detects a stimulus.
 
• Sensory neurons send electrical impulses to a relay neuron located in the spinal cord.
 
• Relay neurons connect sensory neurons to motor neurons.
 
• Motor neurons send **electrical impulses** to an effector.
 
• Effector produces a response.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Receptor→sensory neuron→spinal cord→motor neuron→effector

 
• A reflex arc is a neural pathway that controls a reflex action. Invertebrates, instead of passing directly to the brain, the sensory neuron's synapse in the spinal cord.
 
• This helps in a faster reflex action without the delay that is caused by routing signals through the brain.
 
• The three main types of neurons are sensory, motor, and relay neurons.

questions.question: Lysosomes are known as suicidal bags because of their ________.
questions.solution:
__**Explanation**__:

 
• Lysosomes are known as **suicidal bags due to their Hydrolytic enzymes. **These enzymes can lead to the self-destruction of the cell when the lysosomes burst and release their content into the cell, digesting its components. 
 
• **"suicidal bags" **when referring to lysosomes comes from their **hydrolytic enzymes which facilitate self-destruction under certain circumstances, not from their phagocytic activity.**
 
• While it is true that lysosomes play a crucial role in **phagocytosis, the process of engulfing and degrading foreign particles or pathogens.** this is not the feature that earned them the "suicidal bags" name. It's their hydrolytic enzymes that, under conditions of cellular damage or stress, may be released into the cell, causing autolysis or "cell suicide" 

**So, based on these sources, the answer would still be "3) Hydrolytic enzymes".**

questions.question: Loudness of sound depends upon which of the following?
questions.solution:
• Amplitude is a measure of the size of sound waves.
 
• It depends on the amount of energy that started the waves.
 
• Greater amplitude waves have more energy and greater intensity, so they sound louder
 
• Loudness of sound refers to the intensity of sound waves. It depends of the amplitude of vibrations.

questions.question: When a freely falling object eventually stops on reaching the ground, ________.

questions.solution: Potential energy = mgh, when it touches ground, h=0 so potential energy becomes 0. Kinetic energy = 1/2(mv2), when it stops after reaching ground its velocity becomes 0, hence kinetic energy = 0 Kinetic & Potential energy gets converted into heat and sound energy.

questions.question: Who had used the term "Ecology" first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ernst Haeckel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ernst Haeckel

 
 
• Ernst Haeckel was a German zoologist and evolutionist.
 
• He was a strong proponent of Darwinism and who proposed new notions of the evolutionary descent of human beings.
 
• He also invented many words commonly used by biologists today, such as phylum, phylogeny, and ecology.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Ecosystem: 

All organisms such as plants, animals, microorganisms and human beings, and their physical surroundings interact with each other and maintain a balance in nature. All the interacting organisms in an area together with the non-living constituents of the environment form an ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/377faffe87f801fad37875fa8fe3fd5faa70648e1d3407f7e9052989a44ae655.png] 

Ecology is the science treating the reciprocal relations of organisms and the external world. 

__
 
• The functional unit of the ecological system involves complex actions occurring between its biotic and biotic components.
 
• The term ecology system was first used by Ernst Haeckel​.__
 
• Dr. Ramdev Mishra is known as the father of ecology in India. He founded the International Society for Tropical Ecology in the year 1956.

questions.question: Name the river which is a reason of dispute between India and Bangladesh?

options.text: None of the option is correct.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The dispute between India and Bangladesh regarding the Teesta River is about the water sharing from the river.
 
• The Teesta River is a 315 km (196 mi) long river that rises in the eastern Himalayas, flows through Bangladesh through the Indian states of Sikkim and West Bengal, and enters the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Teesta River originates from the Pahundri (or Teesta Congse) glacier above 7,068 meters (23,189 ft) and flows south through the Gorge and Rapids in the Sikkim Himalayas.
